question: What is the first-line medication of choice for treating a severe anaphylactic drug reaction?

options.A: Diphenhydramine
options.B: Hydrocortisone
options.C: Epinephrine
options.D: Albuterol

explanation: Epinephrine is the life-saving drug that must be given immediately during anaphylaxis to reverse airway swelling and raise blood pressure. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T4#GNS215_U5_T4_h7)

question: What is a flat, discolored skin lesion that is less than 1 cm wide called?

options.A: Papule
options.B: Nodule
options.C: Plaque
options.D: Macule

explanation: A macule is a flat, distinct, discolored area on the skin surface with a diameter of less than 1 cm, such as a regular freckle. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T10#GNS213_U5_T10_h1)

question: Which of these is a common biological hazard you might find in contaminated food?

options.A: Vitamin C supplements
options.B: Natural mineral water
options.C: Pathogenic bacteria like Salmonella
options.D: Plastic packaging materials

explanation: Harmful bacteria and other living microorganisms are biological hazards responsible for most cases of food poisoning.

question: Why is early recognition of occupational lung diseases so critical for patients?

options.A: Treatment only works during the first week of coughing
options.B: The lung tissue scarring is usually permanent once it forms
options.C: Employers will immediately pay compensation before it spreads
options.D: Infections will spread to the brain within a few hours

explanation: Because the damage caused by dust accumulation leads to irreversible fibrosis, catching the condition early helps prevent further exposure and worsening illness. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T8#GNS213_U2_T8_h1)

question: What special type of tissue lines the inside of the ureter so it can stretch?

options.A: Simple squamous epithelium
options.B: Transitional epithelium
options.C: Stratified squamous epithelium
options.D: Simple columnar epithelium

explanation: You're learning fast! Transitional epithelium is amazing because it stretches easily as fluid passes through.

question: Which type of parasitic egg is known for having a little lid (operculum) or a sharp spine?

options.A: Trematode ova
options.B: Nematode ova
options.C: Bacterial spores
options.D: Cestode ova

explanation: Flukes, or trematodes, lay eggs with a tiny lid or spine to help the larva escape. Spot on!

question: Which finding around a skeletal traction pin site means you need to call the doctor right away?

options.A: A small amount of clear dried crust around the metal entry point
options.B: The metal pin is visibly loose or wobbling
options.C: Mild skin redness close to the pin
options.D: Clear fluid drainage during the first day

explanation: You're doing great! Pins need to stay rock-solid in the bone. A loose pin messes up the whole traction setup and always needs a doctor's attention.

question: What is the main reason nurses use a partograph during labor?

options.A: To screen for sexually transmitted infections
options.B: To monitor labor progress and detect deviations from normal labor early
options.C: To calculate the exact date of conception
options.D: To test the mother's blood glucose levels

explanation: You'll be seeing a lot of the partograph in the maternity ward! It's our trusty visual chart to track how labor is going and catch any warning signs early.

question: When did Nigeria introduce its first official National Drug Policy to fix chaotic drug distribution?
explanation: Nigeria rolled out its very first formal National Drug Policy back in 1990 to clean up unregulated drug imports and fight fake medicines.

question: Which of the following is considered a primary physiological need?

options.A: Oxygen
options.B: Financial security
options.C: Friendship
options.D: Personal achievement

explanation: Oxygen is a critical physiological need required immediately to sustain life and cellular function. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h3)

question: Why must a nurse consider a client's budget when planning a diet?

options.A: Nurses are legally responsible for paying for patient groceries
options.B: Hospital policies require all outpatient meals to be low cost
options.C: Expensive foods have zero nutritional value for anyone
options.D: Clients are unlikely to follow plans that feature unaffordable foods

explanation: Exactly! If healthy food is too expensive for the patient's pocket, they won't be able to stick to the plan.

question: Why is the nurse considered the central link in nutritional care for psychiatric patients?

options.A: They hold the legal authority to prescribe all specialized diets
options.B: They are the only team members trained in human biology
options.C: They dictate what medications the psychiatrist must order
options.D: They spend the most time with the patient and monitor daily habits

explanation: Correct! Because nurses are constantly around patients, they are in the best position to track real-time food intake and side effects.

question: What is a major practical challenge to good clinical supervision in busy Nigerian hospitals?

options.A: An excess of well-trained administrative supervisors
options.B: Complete absence of any clinical policies or guidelines
options.C: Heavy staff workloads and severe staff shortages
options.D: Too much free time available during morning shifts

explanation: We all know how packed the wards can get! High patient numbers and few staff members make it tough to find time for mentoring.

question: What is Chadwick's sign?

options.A: A bluish discoloration of the vagina and cervix
options.B: A softening of the lower uterine segment
options.C: The fluttering sensation of fetal movement
options.D: A softening of service tip

explanation: Chadwick's sign is that distinct bluish-violet tint in the vaginal walls caused by extra blood rushing to the area during pregnancy.

question: How can community health nurses best encourage rural women to seek early help for breast lumps?

options.A: By distributing expensive mammogram machines to every household
options.B: By banning traditional healers from practicing any form of medicine
options.C: By engaging local leaders and providing culturally sensitive education
options.D: By waiting quietly in the hospital clinic for patients to walk in

explanation: Working hand-in-hand with village leaders and using simple, warm language builds trust and brings women to the clinic early.

question: A patient has a breathing rate of 32 breaths per minute and an oxygen level of 91% on room air. How is this classified?

options.A: Asymptomatic infection
options.B: Mild illness
options.C: Severe illness
options.D: Moderate illness

explanation: An oxygen level below 94% along with fast breathing means the patient is struggling and needs urgent care. You can totally master this! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T12#GNS214_U1_T12_h3)

question: What is the very first thing you should do right after pulling the needle out of your patient's skin?

options.A: Massage the injection site vigorously with an alcohol swab
options.B: Recap the needle carefully using both hands
options.C: Engage the safety device and drop it into a sharps container
options.D: Place the used syringe on the bedside table for later disposal

explanation: Safety first! Always pop the safety shield on and drop it straight into the sharps box to keep yourself and others safe from accidental pricks.

question: What kind of air pressure is kept in the CSSD washing and decontamination room?

options.A: Neutral air pressure
options.B: Negative air pressure
options.C: Positive air pressure
options.D: Variable air pressure

explanation: Think of negative pressure like a vacuum that sucks air in. It pulls air into the room instead of blowing it out, keeping dirty germs trapped safely inside the washing area.

question: What do we mean by "illness behaviour"?

options.A: The laboratory test results confirming an infection
options.B: The permanent physical damage caused by a disease
options.C: How a doctor chooses the correct medication dosage
options.D: How a person responds to symptoms and seeks help

explanation: Think of illness behaviour as the steps people take when something feels off in their body—ranging from staying home to rest, to visiting the clinic for help. You've got this!

question: Which of these is a common local carbohydrate staple you will see in Nigerian menu planning?

options.A: Olive oil
options.B: Garri
options.C: Apples
options.D: Salmon

explanation: Garri, made from cassava, is a widely enjoyed and accessible energy source right here at home!

question: What is your main nursing duty when giving drugs to stop excessive bleeding after an abortion?

options.A: Encourage her to drink large amounts of oral rehydration fluids
options.B: Watch for the womb to contract and bleeding to slow down
options.C: Check her skin for rashes every five minutes
options.D: Keep the patient flat with her legs raised high

explanation: These drugs work by making the womb muscle squeeze tight, closing off those bleeding vessels. You're doing great with your medication checks!

question: At what age does the posterior fontanelle usually close up?

options.A: By the end of the second year
options.B: 2 to 3 months of age
options.C: At birth
options.D: 9 to 18 months of age

explanation: Correct! Because it's the smaller one, the posterior fontanelle closes early, usually by 2 to 3 months.

question: How is a public corporation different from a standard government ministry?

options.A: It is completely privately owned by foreign investors
options.B: It only provides care to international travelers
options.C: It has more financial autonomy and generates revenue
options.D: It does not have to follow any government regulations

explanation: Think of public corporations as businesses set up by the government. Unlike normal ministries that only use tax money, they are designed to bring in their own income!

question: What is a reservoir in the chain of infection?

options.A: The method used by a microbe to travel to a new host
options.B: The natural habitat where a pathogen lives and multiplies
options.C: The specific entry point through broken skin
options.D: A person who has complete immunity against disease

explanation: A reservoir acts as the home base where germs live, grow, and reproduce before moving to a new host. [learn more](GST114_U1_T3#GST114_U1_T3_h2)

question: What is the primary goal of partner notification (contact tracing) when dealing with STIs?

options.A: To break the chain of transmission and prevent reinfection
options.B: To punish individuals who engage in high-risk sexual behaviours
options.C: To collect financial penalties for public health clinic operations
options.D: To establish legal liability for disease outbreaks in the community

explanation: It's all about stopping the cycle! Treating partners ensures they don't keep passing the infection back and forth.

question: Why are gonadotropin fertility hormones usually given as injections instead of swallowing pills?

options.A: Pills would cause too much stomach upset
options.B: Protein-based hormones are destroyed in the digestive tract
options.C: Injections are cheaper to manufacture
options.D: Injections allow patients to self-dose without a prescription

explanation: Hormones like FSH are proteins that would be broken down and ruined by stomach acid if swallowed as pills. Makes total sense!

question: Why must a client eat a diet rich in carbohydrates for three days before a GTT?

options.A: To make sure the stomach is completely full before drinking the sweet syrup
options.B: To prevent false-positive results caused by low carbohydrate intake
options.C: To test how fast the liver can store extra glycogen reserves
options.D: To ensure the patient has plenty of energy to sit still during the test

explanation: If a patient restricts carbs beforehand, their body stops producing enough insulin, causing a fake diabetic spike during the test. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T20#GNS222_U2_T20_h3)

question: What is the most common way people first catch Lassa fever?

options.A: Being bitten by infected mosquitoes at dusk
options.B: Swimming in slow-moving rural rivers
options.C: Eating food contaminated by rat urine or faeces
options.D: Inhaling dust from sweeping dry sandy floors

explanation: Ingesting food or water touched by infected rodent waste is the number one way the virus enters the human body.

question: Which eye sign is a classic warning sign of advanced Vitamin A deficiency?

options.A: Enlarged goiter
options.B: Conjunctival pallor
options.C: Jaundiced sclera
options.D: Bitot's spots

explanation: You're right! Bitot's spots look like little foamy, dry patches on the white part of the eye, telling us the child badly needs Vitamin A. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T7#GNS313_U3_T7_h4)

question: What is the main goal of different health sectors working together?

options.A: To increase the cost of specialized medical equipment
options.B: To coordinate care and improve community health outcomes
options.C: To eliminate all private hospitals from the healthcare system
options.D: To reduce the total number of practicing nurses in a region

explanation: Teamwork across different health areas helps us share resources and close gaps in patient care. You'll see this often in community postings!

question: Which of these is NOT a good safety practice for emergency equipment?

options.A: Conducting regular staff simulation drills
options.B: Ignoring minor device malfunctions
options.C: Documenting equipment maintenance logs
options.D: Debriefing team performance after code events

explanation: Spot on! Never brush off small faults—minor issues can turn into big failures during a real emergency. Keep up the great work! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T11#GNS321_U2_T11_h5)

question: Why do symptoms only show up a year after a person first gets infected?

options.A: The adult worm takes that long to migrate and approach the skin
options.B: The immune system suppresses all signs until the worm dies
options.C: The larvae remain dormant in the stomach for twelve months
options.D: The parasite only produces toxins after it leaves the human body

explanation: Exactly! The worm takes its sweet time growing and traveling through the body tissues before finally reaching the skin surface. Keep up the brilliant thinking!

question: Which bedside check gives immediate confirmation that an endotracheal tube is correctly placed in the trachea?

options.A: Daily routine chest radiography results
options.B: End-tidal carbon dioxide (ETCO2) monitoring
options.C: Measurement of peak inspiratory pressure
options.D: Arterial blood gas analysis drawn after 30 minutes

explanation: ETCO2 detectors quickly show exhaled carbon dioxide right at the bedside, proving the tube went down the windpipe and not the stomach.

question: A patient asks for a safe way to cook potatoes on a low-fat diet. What should you suggest?

options.A: Baked or boiled without butter or sour cream
options.B: Pan-fried in rich bacon drippings for flavor
options.C: Deep-fried in vegetable oil until golden brown
options.D: Smashed with heavy whipping cream and whole milk

explanation: Exactly! Potatoes are naturally fat-free, but you must skip the added butter, cream, or oils.

question: What is an important advocacy role of a nurse working with displaced populations?

options.A: Voicing the health and safety needs of vulnerable groups to authorities
options.B: Constructing permanent concrete housing units personally
options.C: Managing financial bank accounts for international donors
options.D: Negotiating military strategy during armed conflicts

explanation: Nurses are powerful advocates! They speak up for their patients to ensure decision-makers hear about their health and sanitation needs.

question: What is the primary purpose of a community health nursing care plan?

options.A: To replace all medical textbooks used in nursing schools
options.B: To punish community members who break environmental laws
options.C: To guide practical nursing actions and measure health outcomes
options.D: To serve as a decoration for the office wall of the clinic head

explanation: A care plan is your step-by-step roadmap. It tells you what actions to take, who is responsible, and how to check if things are getting better.

question: Who do we traditionally call a 'patient' in a healthcare setting?

options.A: An active partner who solely directs their own medical treatment
options.B: An individual receiving medical treatment for a disease or injury
options.C: A person who only seeks wellness advice in a community hall
options.D: A healthcare professional working inside a tertiary hospital

explanation: You got this! A patient is simply someone who is dealing with an illness or injury and getting care from medical pros.

question: What is a critical rule to follow regarding promises made to disaster survivors?

options.A: Promise that all their family members are safe
options.B: Tell them the government will pay for everything
options.C: Never make promises you cannot guarantee to keep
options.D: Promise them a new home to make them feel better

explanation: False promises destroy trust and increase anxiety when reality turns out differently. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T6#GNS315_U5_T6_h7)

question: What is the primary function of the dorsal root ganglion?

options.A: It generates motor commands for reflex actions
options.B: It connects the spinal nerve directly to the sympathetic trunk
options.C: It produces cerebrospinal fluid to cushion the nerve
options.D: It houses the cell bodies of sensory neurons

explanation: The dorsal root ganglion is a distinct swelling along the sensory root that contains the cell bodies of incoming sensory neurons. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T26#GNS211_U3_T26_h3)

question: A home care nurse visits an elderly patient who just had a hip replacement. What is the most important safety tip to give them?

options.A: Remove loose throw rugs from all walkways
options.B: Keep all windows open wide for fresh air circulation
options.C: Paint all indoor stairs a bright neon color
options.D: Turn off all lights at night to save electrical energy

explanation: Loose rugs are a major trap for feet and frequently cause falls. Clearing the floor keeps your patient safe at home!

question: Where does the first step of blood filtration happen in the kidney?

options.A: Glomerulus
options.B: Renal pelvis
options.C: Loop of Henle
options.D: Collecting duct

explanation: Great try! Blood pressure pushes water and small particles through a tiny ball of capillaries called the glomerulus to start the cleaning process.

question: Blood from under the tongue flows directly into which major vein on its way to the heart?

options.A: Renal artery
options.B: Hepatic portal vein
options.C: Femoral vein
options.D: Internal jugular vein

explanation: You've got this! The sublingual veins drain straight into the internal jugular vein to reach the heart quickly.

question: Why must surgical instruments be wiped free of blood right after a procedure finishes?

options.A: To ensure the instruments weigh less when returned to central supply
options.B: To prevent the circulating nurse from wearing heavy utility gloves
options.C: To keep blood from drying and damaging the instruments during sterilization
options.D: To make it easier for the surgeon to count them before leaving

explanation: If blood dries up in the tiny joints and crevices, it ruins the instruments and makes later cleaning much harder. Quick wiping keeps them in top shape!

question: Why is malaria prevention especially critical for individuals living with sickle cell anaemia?

options.A: Anti-malarial medications cure the underlying genetic mutation permanently
options.B: Malaria infection triggers severe red blood cell sickling and life-threatening crises
options.C: Malaria parasites feed directly on normal adult haemoglobin A exclusively
options.D: Fever from malaria permanently stops the bone marrow from making blood

explanation: Fever, inflammation, and red blood cell destruction caused by malaria are powerful triggers that induce widespread vessel blockage in sickle cell patients. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h6)

question: Which type of dietary fiber is especially important to include in the daily meals of older adults?

options.A: Low-residue fiber to completely eliminate bowel movements
options.B: Synthetic fiber powders to speed up stomach emptying
options.C: Animal-derived fiber to build stronger intestinal walls
options.D: High-fiber foods to prevent chronic constipation

explanation: Well done! Because bowel movements tend to slow down with age, fiber is a simple superhero for adding bulk and preventing painful constipation.

question: Why do waterborne diseases like cholera often spike during the rainy season in many Nigerian communities?

options.A: Rainfall increases the population of adult malaria-carrying mosquitoes
options.B: Cold weather lowers overall human immunity against intestinal parasites
options.C: Heavy rains can wash surface waste and sewage into vulnerable drinking water sources
options.D: Humidity causes airborne bacteria to multiply rapidly in closed indoor spaces

explanation: Exactly right. Heavy floods easily mix surface waste into community water supplies, increasing the risk of waterborne illnesses.

question: A community health nurse visits a home where a parent recently died from an AIDS-related illness. What is the best first step to take?

options.A: Discharge the family from clinic follow-up to protect patient privacy
options.B: Immediately report the extended family to the police for property grabbing
options.C: Transfer all children to a distant government orphanage home
options.D: Perform a comprehensive assessment of the children's nutritional and social needs

explanation: A complete nursing assessment helps you understand their health, feeding status, and immediate social needs so you can offer the right help. Nursing is all about holistic care!

question: What is the main reason regulatory bodies inspect private maternity homes?

options.A: To dictate the daily menu options for admitted patients
options.B: To ensure compliance with safety standards and prevent quackery
options.C: To collect taxes on behalf of international health groups
options.D: To supply free prescription medications to the facility

explanation: Well done! Routine checks make sure facilities keep things clean, safe, and professional to protect mums and babies.

question: A postnatal mother comes in with a fever and foul-smelling lochia. What does this usually mean?

options.A: Early return of normal menstruation
options.B: Normal involution of the uterus
options.C: Dehydration from breastfeeding
options.D: Postnatal sepsis or infection

explanation: Bad-smelling lochia combined with a fever is a classic red flag for a uterine infection. You'll want to escalate this quickly for medical treatment!

question: Which of the following is an environmental factor that can cause performance deficits?

options.A: Personal family crises at home
options.B: A deliberate choice to ignore protocols
options.C: Chronic understaffing and extreme fatigue
options.D: Willful disobedience of hospital rules

explanation: Environmental causes relate to workplace conditions like high workloads, broken tools, and exhaustion. [learn more](GST321_U1_T22#GST321_U1_T22_h4)

question: What is the main function of the heart valves during the cardiac cycle?

options.A: To prevent blood from flowing backward
options.B: To generate electrical sparks for the heartbeat
options.C: To filter bacteria out of the bloodstream
options.D: To separate the left and right lungs

explanation: Valves act like one-way doors that open to let blood pass forward and snap shut to stop it from flowing backward. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h3)

question: Which of these is a 'push factor' that drives a child away from home?

options.A: Promises of high daily wages from friends
options.B: The desire to escape boring school routines
options.C: The bright lights and excitement of the city
options.D: Severe domestic abuse and neglect by parents

explanation: Think of push factors as negative experiences at home that literally 'push' a child away to find safety elsewhere.

question: Why do sulfonylurea drugs carry a higher risk of causing low blood sugar (hypoglycaemia) compared to Metformin?

options.A: They destroy counter-regulatory hormones like glucagon and cortisol
options.B: They force the kidneys to dump excess sugar into the urine too quickly
options.C: They actively stimulate insulin release from the pancreas regardless of blood sugar levels
options.D: They completely block the liver from releasing any stored glucose ever

explanation: Spot on! Sulfonylureas keep pushing the pancreas to pump out insulin even if blood sugar levels are already dropping, which can cause hypoglycaemia.

question: A client with active breast cancer asks for an injectable contraceptive. How is this classified under WHO guidelines?

options.A: Category 4
options.B: Category 3
options.C: Category 1
options.D: Category 2

explanation: Because breast cancer is sensitive to hormones, using hormonal contraceptives is unsafe and falls into the restricted Category 4.

question: A patient asks for the best protein choice on a low-fat diet. What do you recommend?

options.A: Ribeye steak with visible marbling
options.B: Skinless chicken breast and white fish
options.C: Pork sausage links fried in oil
options.D: Deep-fried chicken wings with skin

explanation: Skinless poultry and white fish are naturally lean and low in fat compared to red meats or fried options.

question: Why is the involvement of traditional and religious leaders crucial when planning community health interventions?

options.A: They are legally required to sign every nurse's monthly salary voucher
options.B: They provide international grants for buying hospital equipment
options.C: They help build trust and dismantle cultural resistance among community members
options.D: They possess formal training in advanced surgical procedures

explanation: Traditional and religious leaders hold massive influence over local beliefs and behavior, making them key allies in overcoming health rumors. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h8)

question: Why is the nurse considered the ultimate safety net for medication administration?

options.A: Nurses are legally responsible for manufacturing safe pharmaceutical drugs
options.B: Nurses have the final authority to change a doctor's prescription
options.C: Nurses diagnose illnesses independently before ordering medications
options.D: Nurses perform the final check before a drug is given to the patient

explanation: As the last healthcare professional to interact with the patient before drug administration, the nurse catches errors made earlier in the prescribing or dispensing process. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T9#GNS223_U3_T9_h1)

question: During a follow-up visit, you notice a patient missed their nutrition goals. What should you do next?

options.A: Discharge the patient from nutrition education
options.B: Reassess barriers and adjust the plan together
options.C: Double the dietary restrictions immediately
options.D: Scold the patient for lack of self-discipline

explanation: You're developing a wonderful bedside manner! Never blame or scold. Team up with the patient to figure out what went wrong and tweak the plan together. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T005#GNS227_U7_T005_h7)

question: Why is checking a patient's 'functional vision' so helpful when planning their daily nursing care?

options.A: It shows what the patient can actually see and do in daily life.
options.B: It determines the exact medical cause of the eye disease.
options.C: It changes the official hospital diagnosis code.
options.D: It proves whether the patient needs surgery immediately.

explanation: Brilliant! Functional vision looks at practical everyday abilities rather than just clinical numbers, helping us figure out the best ways to support their independence.

question: Your patient has chest congestion with thick mucus that just won't budge. What drug class should you expect the doctor to order?

options.A: A topical anesthetic
options.B: An opioid suppressant
options.C: An expectorant
options.D: A loop diuretic

explanation: You nailed it. Thick, immobile chest congestion is the number one reason to prescribe an expectorant.

question: What does male sexual dysfunction mainly affect?

options.A: Upper respiratory function
options.B: Physical intimacy and satisfaction
options.C: Renal filtration capacity
options.D: Skeletal muscle development

explanation: You've got this! Male sexual dysfunction simply means there's trouble with enjoying or engaging in sexual activity. It's all about intimacy and satisfaction.

question: Why do community nurses treat the girl child as a distinct vulnerable group?

options.A: Female children require fewer nutritional resources than male children do.
options.B: The law prohibits male children from accessing primary healthcare services.
options.C: Girls face unique gender-specific social and cultural barriers that affect their development.
options.D: Boys do not experience any health challenges during their childhood years.

explanation: Spot on! Cultural norms and everyday expectations often place extra hurdles in front of girls, meaning we as nurses need to look out for them with targeted care.

question: What is the best diet to start a patient on right after they go home from an esophageal dilation?

options.A: Consume only dry cracker products for the first three days
options.B: Maintain strict total parenteral nutrition for one full week
options.C: Resume regular heavy solid meals immediately to test the stretch
options.D: Start with clear liquids and slowly advance to soft foods

explanation: The lining of the esophagus needs a little time to calm down. Starting with clear liquids gives it a break before slowly moving up to soft, easy-to-swallow foods.

question: Which of the following is part of a psychosocial assessment?

options.A: Checking the range of motion in the patient's knee joint
options.B: Evaluating the patient's coping mechanisms and support systems
options.C: Listening for abnormal breath sounds in the lower lobes
options.D: Reviewing lab results for elevated white blood cells

explanation: Spot on! Psychosocial checks look at mental health, how well the patient handles stress, and who is there to support them at home.

question: What is a main duty of a nurse working in a school?

options.A: Purchasing food supplies for the school cafeteria
options.B: Conducting routine health screenings and managing minor injuries
options.C: Setting the financial budget for local education ministries
options.D: Designing the structural blueprints for new school buildings

explanation: Exactly! School nurses focus on first aid, checking students' health, and handling everyday health needs right on campus.

question: You need cheap gloves for quick, low-risk tasks where tearing isn't a big worry. Which material is best?

options.A: Latex
options.B: Vinyl
options.C: Surgical
options.D: Nitrile

explanation: Vinyl is budget-friendly and latex-free, making it ideal for quick, low-risk chores where you don't need heavy-duty strength.

question: What is the primary focus of nursing care for a cancer patient receiving end-of-life support?

options.A: Testing new experimental medication regimens
options.B: Maximizing comfort and maintaining dignity
options.C: Restoring normal nutritional and metabolic status
options.D: Aggressively treating the underlying tumor growth

explanation: At the end of life, our nursing focus shifts completely to surrounding the patient and family with comfort, peace, and dignity.

question: A pregnant client shares that she drank a local root mix to prevent pregnancy before realizing she was already conceiving. How should you respond?

options.A: Report the local healer immediately to local law enforcement authorities
options.B: Assess for any adverse side effects and provide supportive prenatal guidance
options.C: Scold the client harshly for ignoring modern hospital medications
options.D: Assume the pregnancy is completely unaffected without asking questions

explanation: Always keep a warm, non-judgmental attitude. Check in on her symptoms to ensure she's safe, and give her loving prenatal support.

question: A male patient looks very distressed, but insists nothing is wrong because 'men do not complain.' What is the best nursing response?

options.A: Refuse to treat him until he admits he is feeling emotionally weak
options.B: Ignore his emotional state and focus only on his physical blood pressure
options.C: Acknowledge his distress gently and validate that seeking help is a strength
options.D: Tell him he is acting too sensitive and should behave like a strong man

explanation: Wonderful! Validating our male patients helps break down harmful ideas that stopping to care for mental health makes them weak.

question: After dietary fats are repackaged into chylomicrons, which system do they enter first?

options.A: The pulmonary circulation
options.B: The portal venous system
options.C: The lymphatic system
options.D: The systemic arterial tree

explanation: That's right! Because chylomicrons are too bulky for regular blood capillaries, they sneak into tiny lymphatic vessels called lacteals inside the villi first.

question: What does 'psychological safety' mean for a clinical healthcare team?

options.A: Patients never experience any physical complications or infections
options.B: The hospital building is completely secure against outside intruders
options.C: Nurses never experience high levels of stress during night shifts
options.D: Staff feel safe to speak up and admit mistakes without fear of punishment

explanation: Spot on! Psychological safety means you can raise concerns and admit errors openly because the team supports growth over blame.

question: What happens to disease prevalence if a new, highly effective cure is discovered?

options.A: Prevalence doubles because more people will seek testing
options.B: Prevalence increases because cured patients are counted twice

question: What is the primary goal of aseptic technique in nursing practice?

question: Why is mixing a chemical disinfectant to the correct ratio so important?

question: Why should nurses always ask patients about any supplements they are taking?
