question: Why do red blood cells change into a sickle shape in this condition?

options.A: The bone marrow produces cells with too much iron and water inside them
options.B: Haemoglobin S molecules stick together to form rigid rods when they release oxygen
options.C: White blood cells attack and deform the healthy red blood cells
options.D: Excess sugar in the bloodstream causes the red blood cells to shrink and warp

explanation: When haemoglobin S delivers oxygen to body tissues, it clumps into stiff strands that distort the normal round cell into a crescent shape. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h1)

question: A patient asks how to lower their colon cancer risk through food. What is the best nursing advice?

options.A: Eliminate all forms of dietary fat from the daily menu
options.B: Eat more processed red meat and smoked foods daily
options.C: Increase intake of fresh vegetables and whole grains
options.D: Take high-dose iron supplements with every meal

explanation: Well done! Eating plenty of fiber-rich veggies and whole grains keeps the bowel healthy and protects against colon issues. Balance is key!

question: What is the most common cause of sore and cracked nipples in a breastfeeding mother?

options.A: Natural thinning of the skin during pregnancy
options.B: Drinking too little water during the day
options.C: Excessive washing of the breasts with soap
options.D: Improper latch and attachment technique

explanation: When a baby only takes the nipple instead of a large part of the areola, friction causes pain and tissue breakdown. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T015#GNS226_U3_T015_h6)

question: A patient with HIV can stay healthy and symptom-free for years. What is happening inside their body during this time?

options.A: The virus replicates slowly while the immune system gradually loses ground.
options.B: CD4+ cells are multiplying faster than the virus can destroy them.
options.C: The virus has completely left the body's bloodstream.
options.D: Antibodies have cured the infection permanently.

explanation: Spot on! Even when a patient feels completely fine during the chronic phase, the virus is quietly at work, slowly wearing down their CD4+ cells.

question: What does a fasting blood sugar test primarily measure?

options.A: Baseline blood glucose after food restriction
options.B: Maximum blood glucose right after a heavy meal
options.C: Average blood sugar over the last three months
options.D: Total amount of insulin stored in the pancreas

explanation: The test measures glucose levels when the body has not consumed calories for several hours, showing the true resting baseline. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T12#GNS221_U2_T12_h1)

question: During labor, a first-time mother with a history of Type III FGM is at the highest risk for which complication?

options.A: Complete absence of uterine contractions
options.B: Rapid precipitous delivery within ten minutes
options.C: Obstructed labor due to rigid scar tissue
options.D: Immediate postpartum hemorrhage from the placenta

explanation: The tough scar tissue from infibulation makes it hard for the birth canal to stretch naturally, frequently leading to obstructed labor.

question: What do we mean by 'second victim syndrome' in healthcare?

options.A: A secondary illness caught by a patient while staying in the ward
options.B: Emotional trauma experienced by a clinician after being involved in an error
options.C: The legal penalty given to a hospital following a malpractice lawsuit
options.D: The family member who has to pay extra hospital bills for an injury

explanation: Nurses and doctors who go through a tough adverse event often carry deep emotional pain. We call them the second victims.

question: After giving a subcutaneous injection, which of these details do you NOT need to write in the patient's chart?

options.A: The exact dose and medication given
options.B: The specific site on the body used
options.C: The time and date of administration
options.D: The brand name of the alcohol swab used

explanation: Spot on! You definitely need to log the drug, dose, time, and site, but the brand of your basic prep wipe doesn't matter for clinical records.

question: Why do common pain relievers like ibuprofen (NSAIDs) often lead to stomach irritation and ulcers?

options.A: They inhibit prostaglandins that build the protective stomach mucus layer
options.B: They stimulate the vagus nerve to release toxic amounts of pepsinogen
options.C: They paralyze the pyloric sphincter causing food to back up dangerously
options.D: They directly transform into hydrochloric acid inside the gastric lumen

explanation: NSAIDs block helpful chemicals called prostaglandins. Without them, the stomach loses some of its natural protective mucus lining and gets exposed to acid.

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard nursing duty during a poisoning emergency?

options.A: Collecting and labeling biological samples for analysis
options.B: Synthesizing new chemical antidotes in the hospital pharmacy
options.C: Ensuring personal protective equipment is worn correctly
options.D: Monitoring vital signs and watching for sudden clinical changes

explanation: Nurses monitor patients, use safety gear, and collect labs, but we leave the chemical manufacturing to the pharmacists!

question: Why are narrow-spectrum antibiotics preferred when you know the exact germ causing the trouble?

options.A: They work much faster than broad-spectrum drugs
options.B: They never cause allergic reactions in patients
options.C: They can be taken without water
options.D: They cause less harm to normal body flora

explanation: Spot on! Narrow-spectrum is like a sniper rifle—it hits only the bad bug and leaves your healthy friendly bacteria alone.

question: What happens during the process of syngamy?

options.A: The zona pellucida dissolves completely to allow movement
options.B: The fertilized egg divides into two identical daughter cells
options.C: The polar bodies are reabsorbed into the main body of the egg
options.D: The male and female pronucleus dissolve their membranes and combine their chromosomes

explanation: That's right! Syngamy is that magical moment when mum's and dad's genetic sets finally blend together into one new nucleus.

question: How does uterine hyperstimulation lead to foetal hypoxia?

options.A: It shrinks the size of the umbilical cord vessels permanently
options.B: It prevents the placenta from refilling with oxygen between contractions
options.C: It forces the baby to breathe amniotic fluid too early
options.D: It causes the mother's blood pressure to rise dangerously high

explanation: If contractions are too close together without resting phases, blood flow through the uterine wall stops, starving the placenta of fresh oxygen. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T003#GNS226_U4_T003_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of analyzing epidemiologic data?

options.A: To turn raw numbers into understandable patterns of health
options.B: To replace the need for physical patient examinations
options.C: To make collection forms look neat and professional
options.D: To hide mistakes made during community surveys

explanation: Analysis organizes scattered information so nurses can see where and why health issues are occurring. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T1#GNS313_U4_T1_h5)

question: How does desmopressin help patients with mild haemophilia A or von Willebrand disease?

options.A: It replaces vitamin K stores directly in the liver.
options.B: It destroys abnormal platelets in the bloodstream.
options.C: It stimulates the release of stored clotting factors from vessel walls.
options.D: It dissolves dangerous clots blocking major blood vessels.

explanation: Desmopressin gives the body a helpful nudge, telling the blood vessels to release extra stored clotting factors so the blood can clot better.

question: What does the French (Fr) scale tell you about a urinary catheter?

options.A: The outer diameter of the catheter tube
options.B: The maximum volume of the retention balloon
options.C: The total length of the drainage tubing
options.D: The rigidity of the catheter material

explanation: Think of the French size as the thickness of the tube. The bigger the number, the wider the catheter!

question: Why is a warm, professional attitude especially important when caring for post-abortion patients?

options.A: It speeds up the physical healing of uterine tissues
options.B: Nigerian law mandates specific bedside manners for maternity staff
options.C: Hospital management requires strict adherence to uniform dress codes
options.D: Patients are often vulnerable and fear judgment from healthcare staff

explanation: Because of societal stigma, these patients are often scared of being judged. A welcoming attitude helps them feel safe enough to get the help they need.

question: What is the primary difference between monitoring and evaluation in nutrition programs?

options.A: Monitoring tracks ongoing activities, while evaluation measures long-term impact
options.B: Monitoring is done by doctors, while evaluation is done by patients
options.C: Monitoring only happens once a decade
options.D: Monitoring costs money, while evaluation is always free

explanation: Monitoring watches day-to-day progress, whereas evaluation looks at the final outcomes and overall success of the intervention. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T003#GNS227_U3_T003_h8)

question: Which symptom is a major danger sign that requires immediate medical help after an abortion?

options.A: Feeling slightly tired in the afternoon
options.B: Light spotting that stops after three days
options.C: Mild cramping for twenty minutes in the morning
options.D: Soaking through two heavy pads per hour for two hours

explanation: Heavy bleeding soaking multiple pads in a short time is a red flag for hemorrhage. Always act fast and notify the doctor on duty! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T007#GNS226_U5_T007_h4)

question: What is a common physical risk of giving artificial IV hydration to a terminal patient?

options.A: Instant relief from all body pain
options.B: Complete recovery of kidney function
options.C: Rapid weight gain in muscle tissue
options.D: Fluid overload and swelling

explanation: Correct! Because failing organs cannot process extra fluids well, IV drips can cause painful swelling and chest congestion instead of helping.

question: Which of these is considered a physical workplace hazard?

options.A: Hepatitis B virus exposure
options.B: Toxic chemical solvents
options.C: Excessive industrial noise
options.D: Heavy psychological stress

explanation: You nailed it! Physical hazards include things like loud noise, extreme temperatures, and vibrations that can wear down your health over time.

question: Which of these medications is classified as a long-acting corticosteroid?

options.A: Prednisolone
options.B: Dexamethasone
options.C: Hydrocortisone
options.D: Methylprednisolone

explanation: Correct! Dexamethasone is a long-acting steroid that stays active in the body for 36 to 72 hours. Keep up the great revision!

question: What is the main reason we dry a newborn baby off immediately after birth?

options.A: To remove residual vernix caseosa
options.B: To assess for congenital skin defects
options.C: To stimulate the cardiovascular system
options.D: To prevent heat loss through evaporation

explanation: Wet skin cools down extremely fast in the open air. Drying them quickly stops body heat from escaping so they stay warm and cozy.

question: If you want to find out what a patient has eaten over the past 24 hours, what assessment tool do you use?

options.A: Biochemical lab panel review
options.B: Anthropometric measurement
options.C: Dietary history recall
options.D: Clinical physical examination

explanation: That's right! Asking a patient to recall everything they ate in the last day is a simple, effective dietary history check.

question: What is the main benefit of keeping a clear audit trail in a Drug Revolving Fund?

options.A: It completely removes the need to perform physical inventory counts
options.B: It allows the pharmacy to sell drugs on credit without losing money
options.C: It makes it easy to track financial transactions and catch errors or fraud early
options.D: It ensures that patients receive their prescriptions free of charge

explanation: A clean paper trail is a manager's best friend. It lets you trace every single naira and drug box back to its source, making errors or theft easy to spot.

question: What is the main reason a nurse schedules serial ultrasounds for a pregnant client with sickle cell disease?

options.A: To check if the maternal pelvis is widening properly
options.B: To measure the exact volume of maternal amniotic fluid daily
options.C: To determine the exact genetic subtype of the fetus
options.D: To monitor fetal growth and screen for fetal anemia

explanation: You're doing great! Regular scans help us check how well the baby is growing and keep an eye out for fetal anemia.

question: When should rehabilitation care ideally start for a patient with a disabling injury?

options.A: Only when the patient requests physical therapy
options.B: After all chronic symptoms have completely resolved
options.C: As soon as the patient is medically stable
options.D: After the patient returns home from the hospital

explanation: Starting early prevents stiffness and muscle wasting. The sooner we help them move, the better their recovery journey!

question: How can you easily tell a mild airway obstruction from a severe one?

options.A: The person with a mild obstruction can still cough and make sounds.
options.B: A mild obstruction only happens when drinking liquids, never food.
options.C: Only severe obstructions cause changes in the skin color of the face.
options.D: Severe obstructions can be cleared easily by drinking water.

explanation: You've got it! If someone is coughing or making noise, air is still getting through—that's a mild block. If they can't make a sound or breathe, act fast because it's severe!

question: How does a community diagnosis help in measuring the success of a health program?

options.A: It guarantees that all diseases will be completely eradicated
options.B: It establishes baseline data before the program starts
options.C: It stops the community from asking for external financial help
options.D: It automatically cures chronic illnesses within the first month

explanation: You cannot measure progress or improvement later if you do not know what the health situation looked like in the beginning. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T1#GNS124_U3_T1_h2)

question: What should the nurse apply across the incision after removing sutures to provide extra support?

options.A: Sterile adhesive strips
options.B: Tight elastic bandages
options.C: Thick plaster of paris
options.D: Wet saline gauze pads

explanation: Adhesive closure strips help hold the skin edges together gently while the deeper layers continue gaining strength after suture removal. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h6)

question: How should you position an adult patient's ear before using a tympanic thermometer?

options.A: Rotate it clockwise three times
options.B: Pull straight down and forward
options.C: Press it flat against the side of the head
options.D: Pull gently up and back

explanation: Pulling the adult pinna up and back straightens out the curved ear canal so the thermometer has a straight shot at the eardrum.

question: In HIV care, what do human rights protections mainly guarantee for patients?

options.A: The legal right to demand free housing upon diagnosis
options.B: Total immunity from any future infectious disease exposures
options.C: Automatic exemption from paying any hospital utility bills
options.D: Freedom from discrimination, forced testing, and breached privacy

explanation: Exactly right! Human rights laws protect people living with HIV from unfair stigma, secret breaches of privacy, and forced medical procedures.

question: A patient arrives at the ward after a knife wound to the chest, and you notice absent breath sounds on one side. What condition should you expect the doctor to treat with a chest tube?

options.A: Pulmonary edema
options.B: Pneumothorax
options.C: Bronchial asthma
options.D: Myocardial infarction

explanation: Chest trauma often lets air leak into the pleural space, causing a pneumothorax that needs a chest tube to let the lung expand again.

question: A patient with heart failure needs an IV infusion. What is your most important pre-infusion check?

options.A: Choosing a vein located in the dominant hand for comfort
options.B: Selecting the largest gauge needle available for rapid infusion
options.C: Warming the intravenous fluid bag to body temperature first
options.D: Listening to the client's lung sounds and checking baseline vital signs

explanation: Great clinical thinking! Heart failure patients struggle to handle extra fluid. Checking their lungs and vitals first gives you a baseline so you can catch early signs of fluid overload.

question: Which test measures the exact number of HIV particles floating in the blood?

options.A: Viral load test
options.B: Basic metabolic panel
options.C: Complete blood count
options.D: CD4 cell count

explanation: A viral load test counts how many copies of the virus are in the blood sample. Spot on!

question: What is a very common early sign that patients with developing disseminated sclerosis report?

options.A: Complete paralysis of both legs
options.B: Vision changes like optic neuritis
options.C: Severe high blood pressure
options.D: Total loss of long-term memory

explanation: Keep an eye out for this: inflammation of the optic nerve causing blurry vision or eye pain is frequently one of the very first warning signs of MS.

question: What is the best way to write down a skin problem in a patient's nursing chart?

options.A: Write the single word 'rash' to save precious time
options.B: Provide precise dimensions, color, and anatomical location
options.C: Guess the exact disease name without checking physical signs
options.D: Record only what the family members report about the spots

explanation: Be specific! Writing down exact measurements, colors, and where it is on the body helps the whole healthcare team track changes accurately.

question: Why do babies with chlamydial eye infections usually need treatment that goes through the whole body (systemic), not just eye drops?

options.A: Eye drops are too painful for a newborn to tolerate
options.B: Oral medications work faster than eye drops
options.C: Topical eye drops alone cannot clear the systemic infection
options.D: Systemic drugs prevent the development of fever

explanation: You nailed it! Chlamydia doesn't just hang out in the eye; it can hide in other areas like the throat, meaning oral or systemic meds are needed to fully kick it.

question: What is the single most effective way to prevent hospital-acquired infections?

options.A: Proper hand hygiene
options.B: Using face shields
options.C: Wearing sterile gowns
options.D: Taking daily antibiotics

explanation: Simple handwashing or using an alcohol rub is your superpower against germs. Never skip it!

question: What is the very first step in the MBO cycle within a healthcare organization?

options.A: Conducting the final end-of-year staff performance review
options.B: Purchasing new medical equipment for the wards
options.C: Executive leadership defining broad strategic goals
options.D: Punishing departments that failed previous targets

explanation: The MBO process starts at the top, giving a clear direction that individual departments can then break down. [learn more](GST321_U2_T5#GST321_U2_T5_h3)

question: Which major part of the adult brain develops directly from the telencephalon?

options.A: Cerebrum
options.B: Pons
options.C: Thalamus
options.D: Medulla oblongata

explanation: The telencephalon is the part of the early brain that grows and expands to form our large cerebrum and its two halves.

question: Which condition is a clear indication for using a warm poultice?

options.A: A widespread whole-body viral fever
options.B: A brand new ankle sprain with active bleeding
options.C: A localized boil or deep muscle ache
options.D: An area of skin with complete loss of sensation

explanation: Poultices work best on localized aches, stiffness, and closed infections like boils. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T10#GNS221_U3_T10_h4)

question: What is the primary reason for keeping a functioning suction apparatus nearby during a gastric lavage setup?

options.A: To suck out blood from the esophagus before the tube goes in
options.B: To clear the airway immediately if the patient vomits or aspirates
options.C: To pump air into the stomach and inflate it for better viewing
options.D: To clean the outside of the rubber tube after the procedure ends

explanation: Vomiting is a common reflex during lavage, and immediate suction is critical to keep the airway clear and prevent aspiration pneumonia. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T12#GNS212_U1_T12_h3)

question: Giving an injection or checking a pulse falls under which domain of learning?

options.A: Emotional domain
options.B: Cognitive domain
options.C: Psychomotor domain
options.D: Affective domain

explanation: The psychomotor domain is all about physical movement, coordination, and hands-on nursing procedures.

question: What defines a pre-testicular cause of male infertility?

options.A: A physical blockage within the epididymis preventing sperm release
options.B: A genetic mutation residing directly on the chromosomes inside the sperm
options.C: A hormonal or systemic problem outside the testes that disrupts sperm production
options.D: An infection of the prostate gland that damages the seminal fluid

explanation: Pre-testicular issues originate in the brain or endocrine system before the signal ever reaches the testicles. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h2)

question: Why does hyperglycemia occur in patients with diabetes mellitus?

options.A: Dietary protein is converted directly into simple sugars
options.B: Cells fail to absorb glucose due to insulin problems
options.C: The kidneys actively produce excess glucose from water
options.D: The liver stores too much glycogen and refuses to release it

explanation: Without enough effective insulin, glucose cannot enter body cells for energy and instead stays building up in the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T13#GNS214_U1_T13_h1)

question: Which of these is an ethical dilemma involving money in nursing?

options.A: Deciding which nurse gets to attend a fully funded overseas conference
options.B: Balancing hospital cost-cutting with the duty to advocate for patients
options.C: Reporting a colleague who forgot to wash their hands before a procedure
options.D: Choosing whether to buy electronic tablets or paper charts for the ward

explanation: This is a classic challenge: nurses always want the best for their patients, but must navigate strict financial limits set by management.

question: A patient taking a new antiarrhythmic drug tells the nurse they feel dizzy and lightheaded. What is the best initial nursing action?

options.A: Tell the patient to stand up quickly to test their balance
options.B: Administer a dose of sublingual nitroglycerin for chest pain
options.C: Check the patient's current blood pressure and heart rate
options.D: Hold the next scheduled dose and discharge the patient home

explanation: Dizziness and lightheadedness can signal a sudden drop in blood pressure or a slow heart rate caused by the drug. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T3#GNS223_U1_T3_h8)

question: How does good delegation by a nurse leader show empowerment?

options.A: By shifting unwanted administrative paperwork onto junior staff
options.B: By showing trust in the team's ability to handle important clinical tasks
options.C: By forcing staff to work longer shifts without extra pay
options.D: By removing all accountability from the bedside nurse

explanation: When a leader delegates well, they are saying, 'I trust your skills.' It helps junior nurses grow and take ownership of their duties.

question: A young patient comes in with a racing heart, high blood pressure, and extreme agitation after taking a street drug. Which category is most likely at play?

options.A: Cannabinoids
options.B: Sedatives
options.C: Stimulants
options.D: Depressants

explanation: Spot on! Stimulants rev up the central nervous system, leading to high energy, elevated vitals, and intense jitters or agitation.

question: A patient with a head injury shows unstable vital signs and irregular breathing. Which part of the brain is most likely affected?

options.A: Brainstem
options.B: Cerebellum
options.C: Frontal lobe
options.D: Occipital lobe

explanation: The brainstem regulates essential life-sustaining functions including respiration and heart rate. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T1#GNS222_U3_T1_h2)

question: How do essential amino acids mostly move across the placental membrane into the fetal blood?

options.A: Facilitated diffusion
options.B: Pinocytosis
options.C: Active transport
options.D: Simple diffusion

explanation: Amino acids are pumped across the placental membrane against a concentration gradient using energy, ensuring the fetus gets enough building blocks for growth. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T7#GNS121_U6_T7_h3)

question: What is the main focus of nursing care for a patient with Ebola?

options.A: Administering high-dose broad-spectrum antibiotics
options.B: Placing the patient on complete bed rest without food or water
options.C: Providing supportive care like fluid replacement and symptom relief
options.D: Surgically removing infected lymph nodes

explanation: You got it! Since it's a virus, nursing care is all about keeping the patient hydrated and comfortable while their immune system fights.

question: What is behaviorism primarily focused on?

options.A: Observable and measurable external actions
options.B: Hidden emotional feelings and inner peace
options.C: Unconscious thoughts from childhood memories
options.D: Spiritual growth and personal reflection

explanation: Behaviorism keeps things simple: it looks only at what you can actually see and measure on the outside, rather than trying to guess inner thoughts.

question: How do nurses use the idea of homeostatic imbalance when caring for patients?

options.A: To cure infections without using antibiotics by encouraging the patient to rest
options.B: To reverse genetic mutations that caused cellular metaplasia years ago
options.C: To connect abnormal vital signs and lab results to failing physiological control loops
options.D: To prevent the aging process from slowing down organ system functions

explanation: Spot on! When a patient's vital signs are out of whack, a good nurse sees it as a sign that the body's balancing loops are struggling and need help.

question: Which blood vessels have walls that are only one cell thick for easy exchange of nutrients and gases?

options.A: Capillaries
options.B: Vena cava
options.C: Arterioles
options.D: Arteries

explanation: Capillaries are the tiniest blood vessels. Because their walls are just one cell thick, oxygen and nutrients can easily slip out to feed your tissues while waste slips in.

question: Why is food safety especially important for individuals living with HIV?

options.A: Unsafe food stops the body from absorbing any vitamins
options.B: Contaminated food directly neutralizes antiretroviral medications
options.C: It prevents the sudden development of severe food allergies
options.D: Their weakened immune systems are more vulnerable to infections

explanation: Correct! Because the immune system may be compromised, patients can catch foodborne and waterborne illnesses much more easily.

question: What does the FIFO inventory method mean?

options.A: Financial-In, Financial-Out; tracks daily revenue collections
options.B: Fast-In, Fast-Out; speeds up the delivery of emergency medicines
options.C: Fixed-In, Fixed-Out; maintains rigid pricing for all drug types
options.D: First-In, First-Out; ensures older batches are used before they expire

explanation: Think 'First-In, First-Out'! The drugs that arrived first on the shelf should be given out to patients first, so nothing sits around long enough to expire.

question: Why is building trust with the community so vital during an Ebola outbreak?

options.A: It stops the virus from becoming airborne
options.B: It lets the government cancel travel bans
options.C: It prevents families from hiding sick relatives and encourages early reporting
options.D: It gives clinic staff higher pay

explanation: Correct! When people trust health workers, they bring sick family members in early instead of hiding them, which stops the spread.

question: Why must nurses gently correct unverified medication myths with pregnant patients?

options.A: Fear of medication often leads patients to stop vital treatments for chronic illnesses
options.B: Myths alter the pharmacokinetic absorption rate of oral vitamins
options.C: Misinformation causes the placenta to immediately reject all chemical agents
options.D: Patients will otherwise report the nurse to regulatory boards

explanation: When patients are scared by bad info, they might stop taking life-saving medicines. Clear, warm teaching keeps both mom and baby healthy!

question: What is the main goal of doing an occupational health hazard assessment?

options.A: To identify and evaluate potential health and safety risks
options.B: To discipline workers who fail to wear uniforms
options.C: To check the company's financial profits and losses
options.D: To prescribe medications for non-work illnesses

explanation: The main point of a hazard assessment is to spot dangerous conditions early so we can protect workers before anyone gets hurt.

question: What is the primary definition of dysmenorrhoea?

options.A: Painful menstrual periods that interfere with daily activities
options.B: Infection of the uterine lining during the postpartum period
options.C: Abnormally heavy bleeding during the regular menstrual cycle
options.D: The complete absence of menstrual bleeding for over six months

explanation: Dysmenorrhoea specifically refers to painful menstruation that is severe enough to disrupt a person's normal daily routine. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T6#GNS216_U2_T6_h1)

question: What effect does severe maternal hypertension or pre-eclampsia typically have on foeto-placental exchange?

options.A: It makes the placental membrane thicker to block toxins
options.B: It increases surface area and speeds up nutrient transfer
options.C: It reduces blood flow and decreases exchange efficiency
options.D: It has no noticeable impact on fetal circulation

explanation: Hypertension causes vessel constriction in the mother's uterus, lowering blood flow to the placenta and starving the fetus of optimal oxygen and nutrients. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T7#GNS121_U6_T7_h8)

question: Which sign around a surgical drain insertion site tells you an infection might be starting?

options.A: Normal skin color with slight firmness around the tube
options.B: Clear pink fluid on a dry, intact outer gauze
options.C: Foul-smelling pus and surrounding skin redness
options.D: A small drop of dried blood near the stitches

explanation: Spot on! Redness, warmth, swelling, and foul-smelling pus are classic signs that bacteria are multiplying. Time to alert the team!

question: What is the main reason for setting up an IV piggyback (IVPB)?

options.A: To rapidly drain excess blood volume
options.B: To deliver secondary intermittent medications
options.C: To measure direct central venous pressure
options.D: To provide total permanent nutrition

explanation: An IV piggyback lets you hang a smaller bag of medicine (like an antibiotic) to run alongside the main IV fluid bag without hassle.

question: What is the golden rule regarding organisational strategy and structure?

options.A: Strategy must follow structure
options.B: Strategy changes before employees arrive
options.C: Structure and strategy are unrelated
options.D: Structure must follow strategy

explanation: An organisation always builds its structure to support its main goals (strategy), not the other way around!

question: Which natural response generates heat through rapid, involuntary muscle movements?

options.A: Shivering
options.B: Vasoconstriction
options.C: Sweating
options.D: Vasodilation

explanation: Spot on! Shivering is just your muscles moving quickly on their own to create warmth when you're cold.

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard preventive screening that nurses should promote for women's health?

options.A: Cervical cancer screenings (like Pap smears)
options.B: Daily bone marrow biopsies
options.C: Blood pressure monitoring
options.D: Clinical breast examinations

explanation: Bone marrow biopsies are intense, invasive tests for deep blood disorders—definitely not routine check-ups for reproductive health!

question: When a mother stops breastfeeding and her milk-producing parts shrink back down (involution), what cellular process is mainly responsible?

options.A: Fibrotic scarring of the alveoli
options.B: Hypertrophy of adipose tissue
options.C: Calcification of the milk ducts
options.D: Apoptosis of secretory cells

explanation: Apoptosis just means 'programmed cell death.' When milk isn't needed anymore, the extra milk-making cells quietly tidy up and shut down.

question: What is the main goal of taking medications for osteoarthritis?

options.A: To permanently cure the underlying bone disease
options.B: To stop all systemic autoimmune responses
options.C: To completely regenerate lost joint cartilage
options.D: To relieve pain and improve joint function

explanation: Well done! OA medications are meant to keep you comfortable and moving well, even though they don't cure the root condition.

question: Which structures are removed during a standard Type II FGM procedure?

options.A: The clitoris and the labia minora
options.B: The entire vulva and perineum
options.C: Only the pubic hair follicles
options.D: Only the vaginal mucous membrane

explanation: Type II goes a step further than Type I by removing both the clitoris and the labia minora (sometimes along with parts of the labia majora).

question: Which type of drink should patients avoid right after a tonsillectomy so you can easily spot if they are bleeding?

options.A: Clear water
options.B: Apple juice
options.C: Plain milk
options.D: Red-colored fluids

explanation: You got it! We avoid red drinks because if the patient vomits or spits up, the red color looks just like fresh blood and can easily cause a false alarm (or hide real bleeding).

question: How does the slow block to polyspermy protect the newly formed zygote?

options.A: It hardens the zona pellucida so other sperm cannot penetrate
options.B: It destroys the genetic material of the first sperm
options.C: It closes the fallopian tube shut with scar tissue
options.D: It kills all remaining sperm inside the vaginal canal instantly

explanation: Once the first sperm gets inside, the egg quickly changes its outer shell (zona pellucida) into a tough shield so no other sperm can squeeze through.

question: What is the main protective antibody packed inside colostrum?

options.A: Immunoglobulin E
options.B: Immunoglobulin A
options.C: Immunoglobulin D
options.D: Immunoglobulin G

explanation: Brilliant! Secretory IgA lines the baby's tummy and intestines, giving them a strong shield against germs.

question: You check a mum on her 3rd day after birth. Where do you expect to feel her fundus?

options.A: Completely hidden in the pelvic cavity
options.B: About three fingerbreadths below the umbilicus
options.C: Level with the umbilicus
options.D: Midway between the pubic bone and umbilicus

explanation: You're learning fast! Since the uterus drops by about one fingerbreadth each day after birth, by day three it sits roughly three fingerbreadths below the belly button. Easy to remember on the ward!

question: Why must a prepared sterile field never be left unattended by the nurse?

options.A: Sterile drapes have a tendency to blow away in room drafts
options.B: Contamination can occur unnoticed if no one is watching the field
options.C: Hospital security regulations forbid empty treatment rooms
options.D: Patients might try to steal the surgical instruments

explanation: Leaving a field unsupervised risks unseen breaches in sterility, which compromises patient safety if used. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T1#GNS311_U4_T1_h6)

question: Why do we schedule a follow-up visit a few weeks after starting post-abortion family planning?

options.A: To run routine blood tests for hidden diseases
options.B: To close her medical file and discharge her forever
options.C: To force the patient to buy a more expensive brand
options.D: To check physical healing and see if her birth control method suits her

explanation: Follow-ups let us confirm she is healing nicely and make sure her birth control method is working comfortably for her lifestyle.

question: What is the main reason a patient is given a laxative the evening before an IVP?

options.A: To lower the patient's blood pressure prior to injection
options.B: To clear gas and stool from the bowels for clear x-ray views
options.C: To prevent the contrast dye from causing severe diarrhea
options.D: To empty the urinary bladder completely before morning

explanation: Stool and gas in the intestines can hide the kidneys and ureters on the x-ray film, so bowel cleansing is necessary. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T3#GNS213_U4_T3_h4)

question: Why must community health nurses work closely with WASH (Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene) teams in an IDP camp?

options.A: Clean water and proper sanitation directly prevent waterborne infectious diseases
options.B: Sanitation workers handle the psychiatric evaluation of adults
options.C: Nurses need assistance with ordering hospital furniture
options.D: WASH engineers are responsible for diagnosing clinical malaria

explanation: Good health in a camp relies heavily on clean water and toilets, making teamwork between nurses and WASH teams a must.

question: Where should a nurse document an accidental medication mishap or patient fall?

options.A: Inside the personal diary of the ward manager
options.B: On the front cover of the patient's bed chart
options.C: In a public text message sent to local news stations
options.D: On a separate institutional incident report form

explanation: Incident reports are kept separate from the official medical record to track safety data and improve hospital systems. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T7#GNS112_U4_T7_h8)

question: Besides physical safety, what else helps create a healing ward environment?

options.A: Playing loud music to keep patients awake during the day
options.B: Keeping the lights at maximum brightness twenty-four hours a day
options.C: Allowing visitors to stay without any time limits
options.D: Reducing noise and addressing patient grievances promptly

explanation: You've got this! Healing isn't just physical—lowering stress by keeping noise down and listening to patient complaints makes a huge difference.

question: What is the main job of the upper oesophageal sphincter when you are just resting and not swallowing?

options.A: To stop gastric acid from reaching the pharynx
options.B: To prevent air from entering the digestive tract
options.C: To produce mucus for lubricating food boluses
options.D: To grind up large food particles before entry

explanation: Great thinking! By staying shut when we aren't eating, this sphincter keeps us from accidentally sucking air into our stomach every time we breathe in.

question: Which lab pattern is typical for untreated hypoparathyroidism?

options.A: Low serum calcium and low parathyroid hormone
options.B: Low serum calcium and high serum phosphate
options.C: High serum calcium and normal parathyroid hormone
options.D: High serum calcium and low serum phosphate

explanation: Without enough PTH to boost calcium, your blood calcium drops (hypocalcemia) and your PTH levels remain low.

question: What is one of the main goals of a nurse acting as a patient advocate in reproductive health?

options.A: Prosecuting doctors who violate hospital budgets
options.B: Writing new national criminal codes in parliament
options.C: Protecting patient rights and pushing for fair access to safe care
options.D: Setting insurance premiums for fertility clinics

explanation: As an advocate, you stand up for your patients' rights, fight against unfair treatment, and help them access the care they deserve. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h9)

question: What actually causes avascular necrosis in a broken bone?

options.A: Loss of blood supply causing bone tissue to die
options.B: Failure of the bone ends to align properly
options.C: An aggressive bacterial infection inside the marrow
options.D: Excessive pressure inside a closed muscle compartment

explanation: Avascular means 'without blood vessels' and necrosis means tissue death. When a fracture cuts off blood flow, the bone tissue simply starves and dies.

question: Which task is primarily the responsibility of the registered nurse in home health care?

options.A: Performing comprehensive initial clinical assessments
options.B: Preparing daily meals for the recovering patient
options.C: Prescribing new medications for chronic diseases
options.D: Installing wheelchair ramps and home safety rails

explanation: Registered nurses evaluate the patient's overall health status upon admission and coordinate the initial nursing care plan. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T4#GNS324_U1_T4_h2)

question: How can a nurse best help a quiet 16-year-old feel comfortable sharing her health history?

options.A: Demand immediate answers before starting the physical exam
options.B: Read medical terminology directly from the textbook
options.C: Use open-ended questions and an empathetic tone
options.D: Speak exclusively to the accompanying friend instead

explanation: Open-ended questions and a warm tone help lower anxiety and make the patient feel respected.

question: How does community-based rehabilitation help fight against social stigma?

options.A: By involving local leaders and educating the public about disabilities
options.B: By forcing communities to build expensive private hospitals
options.C: By restricting public gatherings for people with chronic illnesses
options.D: By hiding individuals with disabilities away from public view

explanation: Education clears up misunderstandings. When local communities learn together, they start seeing the person first, not the disability.

question: A patient with a recent stroke begins leaking stool unconsciously. What is the most likely underlying cause?

options.A: Primary infection of the internal anal lining
options.B: Neurological damage disrupting normal bowel signaling
options.C: Complete loss of rectal tissue elasticity
options.D: Severe physical injury to the external sphincter muscle

explanation: Strokes affect the central nervous system pathways that control voluntary bowel function, leading to reflex emptying without conscious control. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T8#GNS212_U1_T8_h3)

question: Why are patients who vomit heavily for a long time at high risk for metabolic alkalosis?

options.A: They eat too many alkaline foods while recovering
options.B: Their lungs trap extra carbon dioxide to fix the fluid loss
options.C: Their kidneys completely stop making urine
options.D: They lose large amounts of stomach acid

explanation: Vomiting throws out hydrochloric acid from your stomach, leaving your body with extra base, which pushes your blood pH up into alkalosis.

question: Which professionals are typically part of the multidisciplinary team for a child with a learning disability?

options.A: Cardiologists, physiotherapists, and dietitians only
options.B: Radiologists, lab technicians, and hospital accountants
options.C: Nurses, educational psychologists, and speech therapists
options.D: Surgeons, pharmacists, and hospital administrators only

explanation: A collaborative team approach involves health and educational specialists working together to support the child's specific needs. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T6#GNS324_U4_T6_h8)

question: Why is a severely low-protein diet generally discouraged for patients with nephrotic syndrome?

options.A: It makes the urine completely stop flowing
options.B: It increases the risk of developing diabetes mellitus
options.C: It causes blood pressure to rise to dangerous levels
options.D: It does not stop protein loss and can lead to muscle breakdown

explanation: Don't worry if this tripped you up! Restricting protein doesn't stop the kidneys from leaking it; instead, it starves the patient's body and leads to muscle wasting.

question: What is one of the most common immediate emotional reactions after an HIV diagnosis?

options.A: Euphoria and overconfidence
options.B: Relief and excitement
options.C: Indifference and apathy
options.D: Profound shock and fear

explanation: Learning one's status often brings a heavy emotional burden characterized by intense fear and shock about the future. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T7#GNS216_U6_T7_h1)

question: A village is turning down a new immunization drive because of heavy rumors. What should you do first?

options.A: Ignore the rumors and continue vaccinating those who show up voluntarily
options.B: Engage trusted community leaders and local influencers to discuss concerns
options.C: Report the community to security forces for refusing public health care
options.D: Cancel the immunization program and shift supplies to urban centers

explanation: Exactly! Working through respected local figures is the best way to clear up misunderstandings, answer questions, and build genuine trust.

question: A pregnant woman in your community presents with a rigid, painful tummy and dark bleeding. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: Ectopic pregnancy
options.B: Urinary tract infection
options.C: Placental abruption
options.D: Normal bloody show

explanation: You nailed it! When the placenta separates early, blood gets trapped behind it, causing a painful, hard uterus and dark bleeding. Keep up the brilliant thinking!

question: Why is keeping things strictly confidential vital for youth-friendly health services?

options.A: Government insurance schemes refuse to pay claims if patient names are published
options.B: Traditional leaders demand exclusive rights to review all clinic patient logs
options.C: Fear of social stigma and exposure will drive young people to seek unsafe, clandestine alternatives
options.D: Hospitals lack physical filing cabinets to store confidential adolescent records

explanation: Exactly! If young people are afraid their families or communities will find out, they'll stay away from clinics and risk unsafe options. Privacy saves lives!

question: A new nurse is sorting waste on a busy ward. Which action shows they are following safety rules correctly?

options.A: Dropping a used syringe directly into a puncture-resistant box without recapping
options.B: Tossing blood-stained gauze into the ordinary office waste bin
options.C: Recapping a needle carefully using both hands before disposal
options.D: Storing expired medications in the ward refrigerator next to patient snacks

explanation: Brilliant! Dropping the used syringe straight into the safety box without trying to recap it is the golden rule for preventing needle-stick injuries.

question: What does proper supervision actually look like after you delegate a task?

options.A: Leaving the hospital premises while work is ongoing
options.B: Taking over all patient documentation duties entirely
options.C: Writing a daily report without visiting the ward
options.D: Guiding, monitoring, and inspecting the performance of the delegatee

explanation: Supervision means staying connected! You check in, offer guidance, and make sure everything went smoothly.

question: What is the primary cause of varicose veins?

options.A: Atherosclerotic plaque blocking deep arteries
options.B: Too many red blood cells being made in the bone marrow
options.C: Sudden arterial spasm from cold weather
options.D: Damaged or weak valves inside the veins

explanation: When vein valves get tired or damaged, they can't close properly. Blood pools in the lower legs, stretching the veins out into those bumpy, twisted varicose lines.

question: What does the term 'cachexia' mean in advanced illness?

options.A: A sudden increase in daily appetite
options.B: Complete blockage of the large intestine
options.C: An infection caused by poor dental hygiene
options.D: Severe muscle wasting and weight loss

explanation: You've got this! Cachexia is a whole-body wasting condition caused by disease inflammation, not just because the person isn't eating enough food.

question: What is a major difference between thoracic spinal nerves and the nerves in the neck or lower back?

options.A: Thoracic nerves only carry sensory information
options.B: Thoracic nerves do not connect to the spinal cord
options.C: Thoracic nerves do not form complex nerve plexuses
options.D: Thoracic nerves lack ventral roots

explanation: While other regions braid together into big webs (plexuses), thoracic nerves stay independent as clean, separate intercostal nerves between the ribs. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T26#GNS211_U3_T26_h6)

question: What is the primary function of the cerebellum?

options.A: Regulating basic drives like hunger and thirst
options.B: Relaying sensory information to the cortex
options.C: Interpreting primary visual and auditory signals
options.D: Coordinating smooth movements and balance

explanation: The cerebellum fine-tunes motor activity and maintains posture and balance during physical actions. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T7#GNS211_U3_T7_h6)

question: What is the normal adult reference range for white blood cells?

options.A: 4,500 to 11,000 per microliter
options.B: 10 to 14 grams per deciliter
options.C: 4.2 to 5.4 million per microliter
options.D: 150,000 to 450,000 per microliter

explanation: A healthy adult usually has between 4,500 and 11,000 white blood cells per microliter. Think of this as your body's standing army ready to fight infection!

question: Which of these is NOT a typical system-level cause of unsafe injections in resource-limited settings?

options.A: Heavy clinical workloads and lack of supervision
options.B: Strict enforcement of international sterilization policies
options.C: Severe shortages of disposable syringes and safety boxes
options.D: Proliferation of unregulated informal medicine vendors

explanation: Strict safety rules actually prevent unsafe practices! On the flip side, equipment shortages, busy staff, and unregistered drug sellers are major drivers of unsafe injections.

question: What is the most common type of skin traction used for lower limb injuries?

options.A: Buck's extension
options.B: Halo-pelvic traction
options.C: Cervical halter traction
options.D: Bryant's traction

explanation: Buck's extension is our go-to straight-pull skin traction for temporary leg injuries on the ward. You'll see this a lot in clinicals!

question: What is the core philosophy of Primary Health Care (PHC)?

options.A: Bringing essential health services as close as possible to where people live
options.B: Focusing treatment exclusively on patients who can pay cash
options.C: Relying entirely on foreign medical aid for community survival
options.D: Building high-tech specialist hospitals in major metropolitan cities

explanation: PHC emphasizes grassroots accessibility, making basic health promotion and disease prevention available to everyone in the community. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T6#GNS124_U1_T6_h6)

question: What is usually the first imaging test doctors use to find a heart tumour?

options.A: Routine chest X-ray
options.B: Electrocardiogram (ECG)
options.C: Complete blood count
options.D: Echocardiogram

explanation: An echo uses sound waves to let us safely peek inside the heart chambers. It's quick, painless, and the go-to tool for spotting masses. Brilliant nursing insight!

question: Which of these crops make up the traditional, local staple foods in Nigerian diets?

options.A: Imported canned beef and biscuits
options.B: Yams, millet, and sorghum
options.C: Processed wheat and refined sugar
options.D: Temperate climate root vegetables

explanation: Spot on! Traditional Nigerian diets rely heavily on locally grown grains, tubers, and legumes that thrive right here in our climate.

question: What is the primary clinical use of a weighing scale in routine nursing care?

options.A: Assessing nutritional status and tracking fluid balance
options.B: Determining skeletal bone density
options.C: Calculating the total daily calorie intake
options.D: Measuring internal body temperature changes

explanation: Weight measurements help nurses monitor nutritional health and detect sudden fluid shifts in patients. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T8#GNS225_U2_T8_h1)
